headline: Indian markets fall for fourth session as surging oil prices and West Asia tensions weigh on sentiment

marketStatus.message: Market is open for trading today.

why: Surging crude oil prices reaching USD 114 per barrel due to West Asia tensions
Geopolitical instability in West Asia rattling Indian equity markets
RBI Bulletin suggesting a broad-based increase in food prices
Negative global cues from US markets and persistent pressure on AI-related stocks
whatHappening: Sensex and Nifty fell for the fourth consecutive session, snapping a two-week winning streak
Nifty 50 dropped below the 22,400 mark after crashing from the day's high
SBI Cards reported a 75% year-on-year jump in Q2 net profit to Rs 778 crore
Jio Platforms IPO saw strong demand, being subscribed 22 times by the third day
summary: Indian benchmark indices extended their losing streak to a fourth day as rising crude oil prices and geopolitical tensions dampened investor appetite. While SBI Cards posted robust Q2 earnings and the Jio Platforms IPO received massive subscriptions, the Nifty slipped below the 22,400 level. The RBI highlighted concerns over rising food inflation while maintaining its focus on price stability and curbing currency volatility.
